Title: Malaysia, Indonesia to set up joint working group to boost rural development
Article:
BALI: Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to establish a joint working group (JWG) to strengthen cooperation in rural development, including through the exchange of best practices in village management in both countries.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is currently on a working visit to Indonesia, said Malaysia could benefit from Indonesia's experience specifically its more structured village rating system to improve data collection and the effectiveness of rural development programme implementation.
He said Indonesia classifies its approximately 75,000 villages into four categories as developed, developing, lagging and severely lagging.
He added that this rating system could serve as a reference for developing an index or set of standards to measure the level of village development in Malaysia, which has about 15,000 villages.
This, he said, would assist the government in planning development programmes more effectively.
"We also aim to have an index or standard for ranking these villages something we have already implemented though their system is more structured.
"We can leverage this to further improve data collection and determine how such data can be utilised for the implementation of government programmes," he told Bernama during a visit to Tegallalang Village here today.
Zahid, who is rural and regional development minister, arrived in Bali yesterday for a five-day working visit to Indonesia, which includes a series of engagements on the resort island and in Jakarta.
He began today's agenda with a bilateral meeting with Indonesia's Deputy Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions Minister Ahmad Riza Patria in which both sides agreed to establish a JWG.
This was followed by the visit to Tegallalang Village and one to Mas Village.
Zahid said another approach worth studying was the Indonesian government's development of ecotourism, for instance, by transforming terraced padi fields as tourist attractions.
Doing so, he said, would see benefits shared not only by the farmers but by the entire village community.
He added that Indonesia also utilises village-owned enterprises known as "Badan Usaha Milik Desa" (BUMDes), which engage in economic activities such as the production of handicrafts for the export market.
He also cited rural development programmes such as "Desa Kirana" and "Desa Lestari" in Malaysia, as well as Indonesia's "Desa Mandiri" (Independent Village) programmes which are similar in nature but differ in implementation.
"By fostering this integration, they can learn from us, and we can learn from them, allowing us to further improve upon what has already been established," he said.
Zahid was scheduled to depart for Jakarta later today to attend the 14th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Management (AMMDM) and the 15th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Asean Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response (AADMER) in Tangerang, Banten.
Meanwhile, Riza said he plans to conduct a reciprocal visit to Malaysia in the near future to study the country's approach to village management and development.
"There is much we can learn specifically regarding the management of villages in Malaysia which will serve as a valuable experience for us," he said.
He also highlighted the need for both nations to collaborate on village development in the Malaysia-Indonesia border regions, not only to strengthen communication ties but also in terms of rural development policy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'He helped anyone in need': A. Samad Said remembered for generosity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Beyond his towering literary legacy, the late National Laureate Datuk Seri Dr A. Samad Said is remembered for his generosity in helping underprivileged youths pursue their education.
National Laureate Datuk Dr Zurinah Hassan said she was among those touched by his kindness, recalling how he agreed to act as guarantor for her Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) student loan when she studied at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM).
"When I was preparing to further my studies at university, I needed a guarantor for my MARA student loan. He did not hesitate to help me.
"Without his assistance, it would have been difficult for me to continue my education. He was incredibly helpful, not only in the field of writing but also in supporting my academic journey," she said during a Bernama Radio tribute programme at Wisma Bernama tonight.
Zurinah said his generosity extended to many others in need, regardless of their background.
"It was not just me whom he helped by becoming a guarantor; there were many others. That was simply his nature. He was an exceptionally generous person who would readily help anyone who approached him in need, regardless of their background.
"If someone came to Kuala Lumpur, he would even offer them a place to stay. He was always willing to help in whatever way he could," she said.
Reflecting on A. Samad's lifelong dedication to language and literature, Zurinah said he frequently reminded young writers to approach their craft with sincerity and appreciate human values.
She said his sincerity was reflected in his consistent efforts to champion ordinary people and marginalised communities through his works.
Zurinah urged younger writers to emulate his perseverance, noting that he produced major works despite limited resources, unlike today's writers who have access to modern technology and digital tools.
"Learn from the struggles of those who came before us. Today, we have many tools at our disposal, including laptops and smartphones, to support our creative work. Make the most of these opportunities to produce even better works," she said.
She said A. Samad's passing was a great loss to the nation, but was confident his lifelong efforts to elevate the Malay language, culture and literature would be carried forward by future generations. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Arthur: Asean's mineral wealth must benefit its people
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asean must ensure its mineral wealth benefits its people, drives innovation and protects the environment as global competition for critical minerals intensifies.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the region's mineral resources and growing economy had attracted global attention.
He said this presented Asean with an opportunity to shape how its resources were developed and ensure its people benefited from them.
"The world is looking to Asean, and for good reason. Our region is blessed with substantial mineral endowments and a dynamic, growing economy. But as we discussed, our ambition goes far beyond just extracting resources.
"Our true success will be measured by the value we create for our people, the innovation we spark in our industries and the care we show for our environment," he said.
He was speaking at the gala dinner for the 11th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Minerals and the Asean Minerals Investment Forum (AMVest) in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
The dinner also marked the fifth Asean Mineral Awards, which recognise achievements in mining, processing and distribution.
Arthur credited the engineers, geologists, technical specialists, management teams and host communities behind the nominated enterprises.
"These awards honour those who prove that commercial success and responsible business conduct are not mutually exclusive — they are mutually reinforcing," he said.
He also highlighted the importance of environmental protection, social responsibility and sound governance across the industry.
Earlier, at the ministerial meeting, Arthur said the global shift towards green energy and the growth of advanced industries had increased demand for secure and diverse mineral supplies.
This placed Asean in a strong position to generate greater value from its resources by processing them within the region.
"To achieve this, we must move beyond being a mere supplier of raw materials.
"We must pivot towards higher-value activities, including midstream mineral processing, advanced manufacturing, cutting-edge technological innovation and circularity," he said.
Asean has developed a common definition of critical minerals and identified a list of 30 minerals to guide investment.
Of these, 16 were identified from the perspective of producers and 14 from that of consumers. This gives the bloc a clearer picture of the resources it can supply and the materials its industries require.
The region is also exploring ways to recover and reuse minerals.
It is working with the United States on recovering materials from discarded electronics and with China on the sustainable use of rock aggregates, marine sand and other construction materials.
Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam are the first three countries to pilot the Investment-Ready Minerals Projects initiative.
The initiative aims to help project developers prepare proposals with sufficient information for banks and investors to assess their commercial viability.
Supported by the World Bank and the Asean Secretariat, the pilot projects will help shape a common set of guidelines and templates in 2027.
AMVest also provides developers with an opportunity to present their projects directly to potential financiers and connect with companies offering the technology they need.
At a joint press conference during the meeting, Arthur said Asean had launched Asean Minerals Connect, a digital platform that allows project developers to showcase their proposals to financiers across Southeast Asia.
The platform is expected to extend these opportunities beyond companies and investors attending the forum in Kuala Lumpur.
"Because while we want to embark on more projects in order to harness the value of the natural resources in our region, first we want to make sure that we do it in a sustainable and equitable manner.
"But in order to do that, our players also need access to financing," he said.
Asean deputy secretary-general for the Asean Economic Community Satvinder Singh said the platform would consolidate information from member states, allowing investors to compare opportunities across the region.
However, countries would retain control over the information they chose to publish.
"When investors want to invest in our region, they need reliable data, reliable information," he said.
He added that the platform was still in its early stages and would become more useful as member states contributed more detailed information.
Satvinder said the importance of bringing industry players and financiers together was evident at AMVest, where investors, mineral companies and technology providers were meeting and exploring business opportunities.
He said such engagement was among the objectives ministers had in mind when they established the forum.
On the impact of geopolitics on minerals investment, Singh said Asean welcomed both Chinese and Western companies.
He added that the region's willingness to work with a diverse range of partners had long helped it remain competitive in the global marketplace.
"We welcome all partners to come and work with us, and we are excited to see a variety of partners coming, engaging Asean.
"I think that has been Asean's strength, and that's what has made us relevant in the global marketplace."

Title: Trump could gain up to US$15mil from Nvidia shares after Huang's return: FT
Article:
WASHINGTON: The spectacular rebound in Nvidia's share price following Jensen Huang's return as chief executive could have added as much as US$15 million to US President Donald Trump's holdings in the stock on Monday, according to calculations by the Financial Times.
Huang resigned on Nov 12 over extramarital affairs including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in the US chip giant tumbling.
News of his return sent Nvidia shares soaring more than 30 per cent and added more than US$900 billion to the company's market value.
According to the Financial Times, Trump may have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of Sept 30.
The newspaper based its estimate on the president's financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics, the most recent of which was filed on Nov 5.
The disclosures do not include precise figures for disposals and purchases of shares.
The maximum figure for his holdings was therefore calculated on the assumption of purchases at the upper limit of each range, and sales at the lower limit.
A report from ABC News, citing Trump's annual financial disclosure report, did not specify the number of shares he owned but said their value reached at least US$12 million by the end of 2025.
It added that his accounts have continued to trade Nvidia in recent months, citing separate filings.
Nvidia said Monday that it had reinstated Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.
Trump said Huang's return followed his own direct contacts with Nvidia's board.
"I've been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it," he told US broadcaster CNBC.
Ruben Gallego, a Democratic senator for Arizona, called for scrutiny of Trump's portfolio.
"We need to investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement," he said in a post on X. "This White House is the most corrupt in history."--AFP

Title: RTM to broadcast special 'Dialog Negara' episode featuring Anwar tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Radio Televisyen Malaysia will broadcast a special episode of the high-impact national discourse programme, "Dialog Negara", featuring Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as the main guest at 9pm tomorrow.
The Broadcasting Department, in a statement today, announced that the 60-minute programme themed "Behind the Decisions" will be broadcast on TV1 and the RTMKlik app, as well as be simulcast on Bernama TV, TV3, Astro Awani, TV AlHijrah, and TVS.
According to the statement, the special episode opens up space for a deeper discussion regarding the considerations, challenges, and rationale behind major decisions made by the government in its efforts to strengthen national development and improve the people's well-being.
"Unlike conventional interview formats, this special 'Dialog Negara' adopts an open dialogue approach that brings together the prime minister alongside the host, a panel of experts from various industries and a studio audience.
"The discussion will focus on four main dimensions: Behind a Decision, Behind Reforms and Change, Behind the People's Hopes, and Behind Malaysia's Future," the statement said.
The department added that this approach allows viewers to understand not only the decisions implemented, but also the deliberation process, implementation challenges, and their impact on society.
Additionally, the programme will feature interactions with figures and representatives from various sectors — including economy, entrepreneurship, health, education, agriculture, governance and related fields — to enrich the perspectives of the discussion.
The department said organising the programme aligns with RTM's commitment as a public broadcaster to empower a mature, fact-based, and inclusive culture of discourse, while serving as a bridge between the people and policymakers.

Title: WTS Capital's Q2 profit rises 18pct on revenue surge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: WTS Capital Bhd, formerly known as Systech Bhd, posted an 18 per cent increase in net profit to RM1.48 million in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM1.25 million a year earlier, driven by higher revenue.
Revenue surged 188.5 per cent to RM48.03 million from RM16.64 million.
The growth was primarily driven by revenue recognition from its ongoing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and computing solutions project, alongside higher contributions from other projects under its corporate solutions segment.
For the six months ended Sept 30, 2026, WTS Capital's net profit rose to RM2.93 million from RM734,000 a year earlier, while revenue surged 530 per cent to RM200.07 million from RM31.76 million.
WTS Capital said it will continue strengthening its project execution capabilities and expanding its range of solutions.
The company will also leverage its customer network and industry relationships to explore new business opportunities across the public and private sectors.

Title: Penang fast-tracks water projects as demand set to rise
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang is accelerating major water projects, including desalination and inter-state water supply, as demand is projected to rise by 27.2 per cent to 1,100 million litres per day (MLD) by 2032.
Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) chief executive officer Datuk K. Pathmanathan said demand stood at 865 MLD last year, with the projection based on feedback from the manufacturing sector, property developers and state development agencies.
He said Penang's limited land area and freshwater resources posed challenges to meeting future demand, particularly amid climate change.
"Penang occupies a land area of only 1,158 sq km. Looking ahead, we do not have sufficient in-state raw freshwater resources to support continuing rapid economic growth in the 2030s, let alone address the threat of climate change," he said in a statement.
The state's main raw water source, Sungai Muda, was also under pressure following increased water extraction by Kedah last year for its "5 Seasons in 2 Years Padi Cultivation Programme".
Pathmanathan said PBAPP had implemented several contingency measures since 2024 to protect consumers against disruptions to Sungai Muda and prevent the Air Itam and Teluk Bahang dams from running dry.
Under the Penang Water Supply Roadmap 2040, the Water Contingency Plan 2030 aims to increase treated water production by 602 MLD, build 4 water treatment plants in Seberang Perai and increase supply to the island.
The state also plans to purchase between 300 and 500 MLD of treated water from Perak under a project targeted for 2032, while exploring seawater desalination plants in the 2030s.
Pathmanathan said Penang's domestic water consumption averaged 267 litres per capita daily last year, 18.7 per cent above the national average.
He urged households to reduce usage to meet the state's target of 250 litres per capita daily this year.

Title: IGP: Tony Pua may be summoned over leaked Pardons Board meeting minutes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have not ruled out summoning DAP leader Tony Pua to assist in investigations into the disclosure of minutes from a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the matter would be referred to an investigating officer for further action.
However, he said police had yet to receive any formal reports concerning the issue.
"So far, no police reports have been lodged regarding the matter. It has only been circulated on social media and other platforms. Nevertheless, the police are prepared to investigate," he told reporters after the conferment of rank insignia to senior police officers.
Earlier, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail directed the police to
mobilise all available resources
to investigate the alleged disclosure of the meeting minutes.
This followed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call for police to investigate the alleged leak and subsequent circulation of the document.
During Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar
denied allegations
that the government had released the confidential meeting minutes to the public.
He also dismissed claims that the document concerning Najib's conditional pardon had been leaked by the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department or the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
Instead, Anwar explained that certain portions of the document had been declassified by the A-GC to facilitate the preparation of responses in legal proceedings brought before the courts concerning the matter.

Title: Anwar pays tribute to literary icon A. Samad Said
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has paid tribute to National Laureate Datuk Seri Dr A. Samad Said, describing him as a literary figure whose works and advocacy for the Malay language and justice would continue to inspire generations.
In a social media post, Anwar said he received news of the
writer's passing
with sadness.
He said Samad's acclaimed novel Salina (1961) brought readers closer to the lives of marginalised people, encouraging them to understand their struggles and uphold their hopes.
"His love for the people will continue to live on through his works, as well as his steadfastness in defending the Malay language and championing justice," he said.
Anwar said he and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, extended their condolences to Samad's family and prayed for strength for those mourning his passing.
He also prayed for Allah's forgiveness for the deceased and that his soul be granted a special place in the hereafter.
"May Allah have mercy on his soul and grant strength to the family he leaves behind," he said.

Title: Man found dead in Nibong Tebal was hit in the head
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: Blunt force injuries to the head were the cause of death of an unidentified man whose body was discovered in Kampung Baru, Jalan Byram, yesterday.
Seberang Prai Selatan police chief Superintendent Jay January Siowou said the cause of death was confirmed following a post-mortem examination conducted at Seberang Jaya Hospital today.
He said police received a report regarding the discovery of the body at the Kampung Baru area along Jalan Byram yesterday.
"The identities of both the victim and the suspect involved have yet to be established," he said in a statement tonight.
It was reported that the body of a man suspected to be a murder victim was found half-buried in mud along an irrigation canal bank in Kampung Baru, Ladang Byram.
A supervisor had
made the gruesome discovery
last night after following bloodstains and fragments of flesh near the irrigation canal.
Jay said police are continuing investigations to determine the motive behind the incident and track down those responsible.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
The punishment for murder is either the death penalty or between 30 to 40 years' jail. Where the death penalty is not handed down, at least 12 lashes of the rotan will be applied.
Anyone with information on the case should contact investigating officer Assistant Superintendent Mohd Rizal Abd Rashid at 019-8282212 or the nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt plans digital access to MyKad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying amendments to allow the MyKad to be accessed digitally, as existing laws do not permit the identity card to be issued in digital form.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the ministry was also looking at integrating passports, birth and marriage certificates, and other personal documents into the MyGov Malaysia application.
He said discussions involving GovTech, MyGov and MyDigital ID were held yesterday following a directive from the Prime Minister.
"...we looked at ways to enable access to the identity card digitally," he said when winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill at the committee stage for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Gobind said users could currently view their MyKad details digitally, but not display the card itself, unlike driving licences issued by the Road Transport Department.
The ministry is integrating government service applications into MyDigital ID before moving them to MyGov Malaysia as a single platform for end-to-end digital services. The next phase will involve integrating payment systems to allow users to renew documents such as passports online.
Replying to Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng), Gobind said the ministry was also exploring the use of artificial intelligence to speed up investigations by the Personal Data Protection Department, which has only 48 staff.
Under the proposed system
, complaints would be submitted digitally, assigned case numbers and referred to investigating officers. AI would help identify potential offences and witnesses to be questioned.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hadi claims non-Muslims turning to Pas over discomfort with DAP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang says the party is gaining support from non-Muslims who are uncomfortable with DAP, which he described as extreme.
He said Pas was confident of defeating Pakatan Harapan in the 16th General Election (GE16), citing the results of recent state elections.
"God willing, we can defeat PH. Look at the 2022 general election (GE15) results, as well as the results in Melaka, Negri Sembilan and Johor.
"These are good signs. It means even non-Muslims are no longer supporting DAP. They disagree with extremism, such as that practised by DAP," he told reporters at the Parliament today.
Hadi also pointed to the poor turnout of delegates at the Selangor DAP convention over the weekend.
On seat allocation between PN and BN for GE16, Hadi said it would be announced closer to the election.
Asked how seats would be distributed in the three Pas-led states, he said it was too early to comment.
"God willing, there will be no problem, whether it's a Pas or Umno candidate contesting. Wait for GE16," he said.
In the Melaka election on Nov 14, BN-PN won 24 of the 28 state seats, while Pakatan Harapan secured the remaining four, all through DAP.
At the Selangor DAP convention on Sunday, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke warned that leaders who were absent
risked losing their positions
and said the party was in crisis mode.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Sabah govt should set up special committee for resettlement of Kampung Pondo'
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government has been told to establish a special committee to oversee the proposed resettlement of Kampung Pondo residents on Gaya island off here.
Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (Star) president Datuk Seri Jeffrey Kitingan said the proposed Pulau Gaya Resettlement and Residents' Welfare Committee should include representatives of the affected residents.
"I understand that most of the affected residents are Malaysian citizens. The government has a responsibility to them," he said in a statement, adding that the relocation could affect families' livelihoods, their children's education and their future.
On illegal immigration, Jeffrey said that his position remained firm, saying individuals found to be staying in Sabah unlawfully must be dealt with in accordance with the law, including repatriation where appropriate.
"Sabah must safeguard its authority over immigration matters. In carrying out that duty, the authorities must respect the human rights and dignity of every individual," he said.
Earlier, Star information chief Anuar Ghani had denied a
viral image of the party
endorsing issuance of identity cards to Kampung Pondo residents should Parti Warisan become the state government.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Arthur gives assurance on environmental safeguards in rare earth mining
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Environmental protection will remain a priority in rare earth mining, said Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup.
He described the mining guidelines as "very strict" and said all applicants must meet the same environmental standards.
"When the mining guidelines are published, it will be very clear that environmental considerations will be one of the ultimate factors that we take into account," he said at a joint press conference during the 11th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Minerals here today.
The assurance follows Malaysia's
agreement on critical minerals
with France, signed last week.
Arthur said the government would hold miners to the standards they could achieve with available technology, citing methods that allow rare earths to be extracted without clearing trees or leaving behind retention ponds.
He said Malaysia had published its export requirements before approving the supply of raw rare earth materials to France for research.
Under the agreement, France will share its rare earth processing technology with Malaysia.
Malaysia has maintained a moratorium on raw rare earth exports since Jan 1, 2024, to develop its domestic processing industry.
Guidelines issued earlier this month allow exports for research and development or processing, provided companies commit to developing processing facilities in Malaysia within three years of approval.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Greatech unit to acquire two industrial complexes in Penang for RM153mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Greatech Technology Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary, Greatech Integration (M) Sdn Bhd, has entered into two separate sale and purchase agreements with Penfabric Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of two industrial complexes in Phase 3 Bayan Lepas Free Industrial Zone, Bayan Lepas, Penang for a total consideration of RM153 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the acquisitions comprise the first industrial complex for RM63 million and the second for RM90 million.
Greatech Technology said the proposed acquisition represents a strategic investment by the group in acquiring industrial properties strategically located within the Bayan Lepas Free Industrial Zone, Penang, which is an established industrial hub.
"With customers' projected demand continuing to increase, the group anticipates that its currently planned production capacity may not be sufficient to fully meet demand in the near future.
"The proposed acquisition will allow the group to enhance its manufacturing capacity in line with anticipated customer requirements and expected returns," it said.
The proposed acquisition is not expected to have any material immediate effect on the group's earnings and earnings per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, it added.

Title: Jetour Malaysia assembles 10,000 vehicles, expand regional export footprint
Article:
JETOUR has assembled more than 10,000 vehicles in Malaysia since starting production in 2025, as the Chinese automaker begins exporting vehicles from the country.
Its first overseas shipment comprised the Jetour Dashing, marking the start of its export operations from Malaysia.
The company is targeting additional markets in Asia, South America and Africa in 2027, with estimated export volumes of about 7,000 vehicles next year.
The exports are expected to position Malaysia as a manufacturing and distribution base for Jetour's right-hand-drive markets.
Since starting local assembly in 2025, Jetour has introduced five locally assembled models – the Dashing, VT9, T1, T2 and T2 i-DM.
Apart from manufacturing, the company has established a local research and development (R&D) team as part of its broader Asia-Pacific operations.
Jetour Malaysia chief executive officer Fu Yong said Malaysia was important to the company's long-term development in the Asia-Pacific region.
"Malaysia is an important part of Jetour's long-term development in the Asia-Pacific region. We see strong value in building local expertise and capabilities here, particularly as the automotive industry continues to evolve.
"Having a presence across manufacturing and R&D allows us to develop a deeper understanding of regional market needs and strengthen the foundation for our continued growth," he said.
Jetour said Malaysia will continue to support its manufacturing, export and technical operations across the region.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Macron's visit puts RM600mil heritage restoration in new light
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The RM600 million allocation to restore the Sultan Abdul Samad Building complex and Carcosa Seri Negara, which was previously questioned in Parliament, has taken on a different perspective following French President Emmanuel Macron's recent visit to Kuala Lumpur.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the public response to Macron's visit highlighted the value of investing in heritage conservation and preserving the capital's historical identity.
Recalling the parliamentary debate when Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim first announced the allocation, she said the spending had drawn criticism from lawmakers.
"I remember the painful discussion in Parliament when the prime minister first announced that he would spend RM600 million to restore the Sultan Abdul Samad Building. Everyone said, 'What a waste of money'.
"But today, people can see the completed projects. When the French President came, people could see the results. What a great way to spend RM600 million," she said.
Speaking at the Kuala Lumpur Festival 2027 announcement and partners' reception today, Yeoh said the decision to receive Macron at Dataran Merdeka, with the Sultan Abdul Samad Building as its backdrop, was deliberate.
"We could have taken them to any of our newer buildings and attractions, but we deliberately chose Sultan Abdul Samad for a purpose," she said.
She said the visit, which attracted widespread attention on social media, had also drawn attention to other parts of the capital, including Pasar Seni and Medan Pasar, rather than focusing solely on its modern buildings and developments.
Yeoh said Kuala Lumpur's growth should not come at the expense of its heritage, adding that historic landmarks must remain part of the city's identity as it continued to develop.
She said the government wanted younger generations to understand Kuala Lumpur's history, enjoy its public spaces and develop a sense of belonging to the city.
Restoring heritage buildings and bringing them back to life would also help make the capital a more attractive destination for international visitors, she added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sum Technology secures RM48mil data centre subcontract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sum Technology Bhd has secured a subcontract for a data centre project in Selangor with a provisional contract value of approximately RM48 million.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said its wholly owned subsidiary, Sum Technic Sdn Bhd, accepted the letter of award to provide mechanical, electrical, process utilities and firefighting subcontracting works.
"The details of the customer and ownership of the data centre have not been disclosed due to a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) signed between Sum Technic and the customer.
"The contract's commencement and completion dates have not been finalised at this stage," it said.
The contract is expected to contribute positively to the group's earnings and net assets per share for the financial years ending Dec 31, 2026, onwards until the project is completed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia still weighing whether to export rare earth elements to China
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is still considering an application to export rare earth carbonates to China, said Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup.
He said Malaysia had previously exported rare earth carbonates to China but that shipments had since stopped while some exports to the United States had been approved.
"We are still considering whether it will continue," he said when asked if exports to China would resume.
Arthur was speaking at a joint press conference with Asean Economic Community deputy secretary-general Satvinder Singh during the 11th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Minerals here today.
On Oct 27, the media reported DTEC Mineral and Metal Technology, a US majority-owned company, had secured a permit to export up to 700 tonnes of rare earth carbonate from Perak to the US for research.
It was the first approval under Malaysia's revised export rules, according to the company.
Malaysia has maintained a moratorium on exports of raw, unprocessed rare earth materials since Jan 1, 2024, to develop its domestic processing industry.
The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry said the moratorium would remain in force through 2027 and continue in the medium term thereafter.
Guidelines released earlier this month allow conditional exports for research and development or processing, provided companies commit to developing processing facilities in Malaysia within three years of export approval.
Asked about the influence of geopolitics on mineral investment, Satvinder said the bloc welcomed both Chinese and Western companies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mazda CX-5 grows up, putting family first
Article:
THE third-generation Mazda CX-5 arrives with a bigger body, a more spacious cabin and a renewed focus on comfort.
But it is behind the wheel where the Japanese sport utility vehicle (SUV) has the opportunity to make its strongest impression.
Now in its third generation, the CX-5 retains the familiar Mazda emphasis on driver engagement while addressing some of the predecessor's practical shortcomings, particularly rear passenger accommodation and luggage capacity.
For Malaysian motorists who regularly travel between cities, navigate winding trunk roads or spend long hours on highways, these changes could make the latest model a more compelling family companion.
The new CX-5 is offered locally in a single 2.5G High variant, with a choice of a standard roof or a panoramic sunroof, and is fully imported from Japan.
Prices start at RM168,510, rising to RM171,510 for the panoramic sunroof version, before insurance.
More Muscle, Familiar Character
Under the bonnet is a naturally aspirated 2.5-litre Skyactiv-G four-cylinder petrol engine producing 185hp at 6,000rpm and 257Nm of torque at 4,000rpm.
Power is channelled to the front wheels through a six-speed automatic transmission.
While the Malaysian version does not receive the mild-hybrid powertrain offered in some other markets, the conventional petrol engine and automatic gearbox retain a familiar mechanical approach.
The output is adequate for everyday driving, although the CX-5 is not positioned as a performance SUV.
Its appeal lies more in delivering predictable power delivery and a balanced driving experience than in outright acceleration.
Mazda's G-Vectoring Control Plus system also works in the background to adjust engine torque and braking responses during cornering, helping the vehicle maintain stability and a more settled trajectory.
Finding Rhythm On Highways
On highways, the CX-5's larger dimensions and longer wheelbase should contribute to a more planted and composed driving character.
At 2,815mm, the wheelbase is 115mm longer than that of the outgoing generation, while the overall length has increased by the same amount to 4,690mm.
The additional footprint is particularly relevant during extended journeys, where a vehicle's ability to remain settled over changing road surfaces can make a difference to passenger comfort.
The naturally aspirated engine delivers its power progressively, rather than relying on a sudden surge of turbocharged torque.
Drivers looking for immediate acceleration may find the character less urgent, but the conventional six-speed automatic offers a familiar and straightforward response.
For highway overtaking, some planning is still necessary, particularly when carrying a full load of passengers and luggage.
The six-speed transmission can be operated manually through the gear selector, although paddle shifters are not provided.
Mazda Radar Cruise Control, with Cruising and Traffic Support, adds another layer of assistance during longer journeys.
It helps manage following distance and supports the driver in traffic, reducing some of the workload on congested expressways.
These systems remain driver aids rather than substitutes for attentive driving.
Trunk Roads Put Handling To The Test
The CX-5's more interesting proposition is how it balances comfort with driver involvement when the road becomes less predictable.
Malaysia's trunk roads often present a mixture of long sweeping bends, tighter corners, uneven surfaces and occasional changes in road elevation.
Such conditions place different demands on an SUV compared with the relatively predictable environment of an expressway.
Mazda has retained its driver-focused approach, with G-Vectoring Control Plus designed to make steering transitions feel more progressive and the vehicle more settled through corners.
The system works alongside the electronic stability control and suspension setup, rather than attempting to turn the CX-5 into a sports car.
Its front MacPherson strut and rear multi-link suspension arrangement is a conventional configuration for the segment, but one that gives Mazda room to balance handling response with everyday ride comfort.
The 19-inch wheels and 225/55 tyres also give the SUV a substantial road presence, although actual ride comfort over broken surfaces will depend on road conditions and tyre pressures.
On undulating routes, the longer wheelbase should help provide a more reassuring sense of stability, while the elevated driving position gives the driver a clearer view of surrounding traffic.
More Room For Family
Beyond the driving experience, the new CX-5 makes a significant improvement in practicality.
The longer wheelbase creates additional cabin space, particularly for rear passengers, while the wider and taller body gives the SUV a more substantial footprint.
Luggage capacity has increased to 583 litres, up from 442 litres in the previous generation.
That additional 141 litres is useful for families who regularly travel with several suitcases, shopping bags or recreational equipment.
The rear seats can also be folded in a 40:20:40 configuration, allowing longer items to be carried without sacrificing all rear passenger seating.
The wider rear door openings should also make entry and exit easier, particularly for families travelling with younger passengers.
Technology Takes Centre Stage
Inside, the biggest change is the redesigned dashboard, which adopts a more minimalist layout dominated by a 12.9-inch infotainment touchscreen.
The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, while a 10.25-inch digital instrument cluster and head-up display provide additional driving information.
A 12-speaker Bose sound system, wireless charger, ventilated powered front seats and dual-zone air-conditioning add to the cabin's comfort credentials.
The extensive i-Activsense safety package includes blind spot monitoring, lane departure warning, lane-keeping assistance, emergency lane keeping, driver monitoring and front and rear autonomous emergency braking.
Seven airbags and a 360-degree camera system are also included.
Putting family first
The third-generation CX-5 reflects Mazda's growing emphasis on making its SUVs more accommodating for family life, without losing the driving characteristics that have long defined the brand.
The larger cabin, improved rear passenger space and expanded 583-litre luggage compartment address practical needs that become increasingly important when travelling with family, particularly on longer highway journeys and weekend drives along Malaysia's trunk roads.
The additional safety and convenience technologies also reinforce this direction, giving drivers greater assistance while making journeys more comfortable for everyone on board.
At a starting price of RM168,510.40, the new CX-5 is not the most affordable option in its segment.
But Mazda's proposition goes beyond engine specifications and equipment lists.
It is about delivering an SUV that brings together driving enjoyment, everyday practicality and family comfort.

Title: Rethinking EV motorsport: Grassroots autocross as Malaysia's high-tech incubator
Article:
WHENEVER the conversation turns to electric vehicle motorsport, the mind almost instinctively wanders toward multi-million-dollar spectacles: carbon-fibre Formula E single-seaters zipping around temporary city circuits, bespoke electric hypercars conquering global hillclimbs, or Le Mans-conquering hybrids that only the big manufacturers can afford to build and race.
To the average Malaysian independent garage owner or paddock mechanic, these high-end racing series feel like science fiction - impressive to watch on television, but entirely irrelevant to their daily livelihood.
Yet, these workshop owners are the ones who desperately need to upskill their talent if they want to remain relevant as the world goes electric, and there is no faster way to learn new skills than in motorsports.
If Malaysia is serious about upskilling its technical workforce for the electrified era, we need to start encouraging a new class of competitors: a separate hybrid class should be created for all levels of motorsport activities.
In fact, the government, through the Motorsports Association of Malaysia (MAM), must encourage hybrid class entries by setting aside prize money for organisers who are willing to go the extra mile.
With grassroots motorsports, we should focus on low-cost and accessible forms of racing - primarily Time Attack, Autocross, or Gymkhana.
The Right Discipline For The Job
Why Autocross? Because unlike high-speed circuit endurance racing, which places immense thermal strain on battery packs and requires massive cooling budgets, Autocross operates in short, intense bursts on closed tarmac lots or kart tracks.
A typical Autocross run lasts between 60 to 90 seconds.
It tests low-speed chassis balance, immediate torque delivery, regenerative braking calibration, and rapid thermal management under peak discharge cycles.
Crucially, it is also a discipline with a low barrier to entry.
The Motorsports Association of Malaysia regulations allow Autocross participation without requiring expensive full-welded roll cages, dedicated racing fuel systems, or specialised pit crews.
It is a sport where a street-legal car, a certified helmet, and a focused driver can compete safely and affordably.
Unlocking A Decade Of "Legacy" Hybrids
The second misconception about electrified motorsport is that it requires brand-new, six-figure battery electric vehicles.
Malaysia already possesses a vast, underutilised fleet of 10-15-year-old hybrid cars sitting in used car lots and independent workshops across the country.
First- and second-generation Honda Jazz Hybrids, Civic Hybrids, CR-Zs, and Toyota Prius or Prius C models are now accessible on the secondary market for modest sums.
Add to this existing pool the modern wave of affordable electrified offerings - from modern mild-hybrids to national entries like the Proton e.Mas series and Perodua's upcoming electrified platforms - and you have the making of a vibrant, multi-tiered grid.
For an independent garage, taking a decade-old hybrid or a modern budget EV and prepping it for an Autocross competition is the ultimate hands-on classroom.
To make an electrified car competitive in a timed slalom, a mechanic cannot simply bolt on an aftermarket exhaust or swap out a camshaft.
They are forced to engage directly with high-voltage battery cooling, inverter parameters, brake-by-wire feel, weight distribution, and energy recovery strategies.
Prize Money As A TVET Catalyst
Mechanics do not learn high-voltage diagnostics by reading government whitepapers or attending passive lectures.
They learn when there is a lap time to beat, a rival workshop in the next pit bay, and actual prize money on the line.
This is where public policy and agencies like the Ministry of Youth and Sports, MARii, or local automotive councils should step in.
Instead of sinking millions of ringgit into hosting foreign sanctioning bodies or high-end international race events that yield little trickle-down technical knowledge, a fraction of that budget could fund a national Electrified Autocross & Time Attack Championship.
By offering meaningful prize purses across distinct categories - such as Legacy Hybrid, Production PHEV, and Open EV - the government can create a direct financial incentive for independent workshops to participate.
To win, garage crews will naturally seek out high-voltage safety certifications, learn how to safely isolate traction batteries, reprogram power management units, and optimise thermal management.
Without realising it, racing converts neighborhood mechanics into certified, high-voltage-capable technicians - building the exact workforce required to service Malaysia's future electrified fleet.
From The Paddock To The Workshop Floor
The transition to electric and hybrid vehicles is often discussed in terms of charging infrastructure and showroom incentives.
But the long-term success of Malaysia's automotive sector rests on the hands that will maintain, repair, and engineer these vehicles once the warranty expires.
We do not need a glitzy, high-cost EV racing series to prove our technological credentials.
By embracing grassroots Autocross as an educational incubator, we can turn carparks and kart tracks into high-voltage laboratories - proving that the fastest way to upskill Malaysia's automotive workforce is through a set of cones, a stopwatch, and a checkered flag.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NexG Bina's bank freeze lifted
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: NexG Bina Bhd says the freeze imposed on certain bank accounts maintained by the company and its subsidiaries with RHB Bank Bhd has been lifted by the relevant authorities.
"The freezing imposed on certain bank accounts has been lifted by the relevant authorities," it said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
The company did not specify the number of bank accounts that had been unfrozen.
NexG Bina had previously disclosed on March 10 that 16 bank accounts belonging to the group had been frozen since mid-November 2025 by the police's anti-money laundering investigation team.
At the time, the company said it had not received any formal freezing order and only became aware of the situation after it was unable to make certain operating payments.
The company's shares ended 16.67 per cent or half a sen higher at 3.5 sen, with 21.85 million shares changing hands, valuing the company at RM43.14 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar reflects on four years in office: More to be done for Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim reflected on his four years in office, acknowledging that much remains to be done to improve the lives of Malaysians.
In a social media post today marking the fourth anniversary of his swearing-in, Anwar recalled taking office amid economic pressures, limited national finances and rising cost of living.
"Four years is not a short period; yet, I still recall the immense weight of this responsibility at a time when the nation faced a multitude of challenges.
"The economy was under pressure, the nation's fiscal position was constrained, and the people were struggling with the rising cost of living."
Anwar said deep-rooted weaknesses in governance and entrenched practices of corruption demanded bold action and reforms.
"Since the first day I stepped into Perdana Putra, my resolve has been to restore the country and improve the lives of the people.
"It has not been an easy journey, but this responsibility must continue to be shouldered with full commitment," he said.
Anwar said the government had, over the past four years, worked to strengthen the country's financial position, improve governance, push institutional reforms and reinforce public welfare.
However, he said there was still a long journey ahead, with much more that needed to be achieved.
"I am fully aware that the true measure of a nation's progress lies in whether the lives of every family have improved, whether livelihoods are more secure, and whether the future of our children is better safeguarded.
"That is what we are fighting for. With the foundation we have established, I am confident that we can go even further in alleviating the burdens of the people and creating more equitable space and opportunities for all," he said.
Anwar thanked Malaysians for their patience, feedback, prayers and continued trust, pledging to give his best to the country for as long as he remained entrusted with the responsibility.
"Prime ministers may come and go, but the well-being of the people must always be priority/championed, and the dignity of the nation must always be upheld," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Girl, 7, killed in four-vehicle crash on NSE near Kempas
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 7-year-old girl was killed after a Mercedes-Benz crashed into a Perodua Myvi, triggering a chain collision involving four vehicles on the North-South Expressway near Kempas.
The child, who was travelling in the Myvi with her 34-year-old mother, died at the scene after the car was pushed forward and crashed into another vehicle and a lorry at Km6.4 of the southbound lane of the expressway.
Johor Baru North police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrol Anuar Nor said preliminary investigations found that the Mercedes, driven by a 58-year-old man, had gone out of control before crashing into the rear of the Myvi.
"The impact caused the Myvi to move forward and hit the rear of a  Chery Tiggo, driven by a 72-year-old man, and a lorry driven by a 50-year-old man," he said in a statement today.
Azrol said the Myvi driver sustained head, hand and leg injuries and was taken to Sultanah Aminah Hospital, while the other three drivers were unhurt.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing death by driving reckless or dangerous driving, which provides for a jail term of between five and 10 years and a fine of RM20,000 to RM50,000 upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US blacklists Megaspeed, two Malaysian firms over AI chip diversion risk
Article:
SINGAPORE: US authorities have barred Singapore-based tech group Megaspeed International from purchasing advanced chips in the fallout from an alleged Chinese espionage scandal surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Here are key facts about Megaspeed – whose former executive Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese spy and said to have had an affair with the Nvidia boss – and its regional network of subsidiaries and affiliated businesses.
- INVESTIGATIONS -
Megaspeed touts itself as a company at the heart of the artificial intelligence revolution, using Nvidia's advanced silicon chips to power high-performance computing inside vast data centres.
The cloud computing company previously led by Alice Huang – who is no relation to Jensen – was investigated by Singapore in 2025 over potential export control violations.
The United States is investigating Megaspeed on allegations it had allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers, circumventing US export restrictions under the guise of acquiring hardware for its Southeast Asia data hubs.
Beijing has denied allegations of spying, and Megaspeed said it was investigating if it had complied with export controls on the sensitive chips.
- TRADE RESTRICTIONS -
On Monday, as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, the US Commerce Department added Megaspeed International, its parent company and subsidiaries in Malaysia and Thailand to the trade blacklist.
Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore was working with the United States to stop companies "exploiting" the city-state – a global transhipment hub – for illegal chip transfers.
Neighbouring Malaysia, which was investigating Megaspeed's local subsidiary Speedmatrix for possible diversion of AI chips, advised data centres on Monday to cut links with US-blacklisted firms.
- EMPTY OFFICES -
At Megaspeed's office in the heart of the Singapore business district, no staff could be seen behind its locked glass doors. Neighbours told AFP they had not seen anyone come or go for months.
The registered address of a company listed as Megaspeed (Thailand) was a two-desk office in a coworking space in central Bangkok, which showed little sign of activity when AFP visited on Tuesday.
- MSFUSION: MALAYSIA DATA CENTRE -
Another company, MSFusion, was also added to the US blacklist.
Corporate records show it shares a common director with Megaspeed in Singapore, but is owned by a holdings company in the Cayman Islands.
MSFusion has bought land to build a data centre in Malaysia's southern state of Johor, according to the company that sold the plot, with other documents pointing to MSFusion's involvement in its development.
When AFP recently visited the site, there were no signs mentioning MSFusion's involvement in the project.
A security post is stationed outside the compound, surrounded by low concrete walls with metal gates.
MSFusion has denied any "equity relationship" with Megaspeed International and its subsidiaries, saying that the firms "operate as separate and independent legal entities."
- SPEEDMATRIX: MEGASPEED SUBSIDIARY -
Megaspeed International has two subsidiaries in Malaysia: Megaspeed International Sdn Bhd and Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, both involved in data processing activities.
Speedmatrix "is a tenant at data centres in Malaysia" that can bring its own servers and AI chips into the country but cannot export them, according to the Malaysian trade ministry.
Speedmatrix, believed to be operating out of the Sedenak Tech Park in Johor, was also added to the US list.
Speedmatrix, Singapore-based Megaspeed International and MSFusion share a common director, Tan Yong Pong, according to corporate papers.
Speedmatrix, MSFusion and Malaysia-based Megaspeed International Sdn Bhd share Ang Kong Siang as company secretary, as well as the same registered address in Johor state, documents show.
- SEIZED SHIPMENTS -
Malaysian customs intercepted at least five illicit shipments of high-end chips from "one Asian country to another" this year, authorities have said.
After one of the raids at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport, AFP correspondents spotted the Nvidia logo on a picture of the confiscated goods.
AFP correspondents also saw a waybill on one of the confiscated containers, with the destination given as SZX – the code for Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in China.-AFP

Title: Three Tangkak students to be charged tomorrow over bullying of schoolmate
Article:
TANGKAK: Three male students will be charged in court tomorrow over the assault of a 14-year-old at a secondary school in the district.
Deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Jamellulkamal Abdul Halim said the investigation papers were completed and referred to the state prosecution director's office.
"The office directed that all three suspects be charged under Section 323 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, for voluntarily causing hurt with common intention," he said in a statement.
The charge carries a maximum jail term of a year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
The victim was allegedly assaulted by three male students at 8am in the secondary school classroom on Nov 13, with a police report lodged the following day.
The assault is believed to have
stemmed from a misunderstanding
over messages in a WhatsApp group.
His parents rushed to the school after they were informed that he had a stomachache. They were shocked to find him
trembling in pain
, allegedly after he was assaulted.
Jamellulkamal cautioned the public against spreading unverified information or making statements that could reveal the identities of the children involved.

Title: Berjaya Food to exit loss-making Kenny Rogers, retain 5pct stake
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Berjaya Food Bhd is restructuring its loss-making Kenny Rogers Roasters business in Malaysia by transferring its operations to a new joint venture (JV) company.
Berjaya Food said it will retain a five per cent stake.
The exercise is expected to result in an estimated gain of RM4.51 million, mainly arising from the termination of lease obligations associated with the business.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Berjaya Food said its wholly-owned subsidiary Berjaya Roasters (M) Sdn Bhd entered into a joint venture and shareholders' agreement with Samaya Food Investments LLC, Vertix Holdings LLC and Nabil Shaukat Butt on Nov 23.
Samaya and Vertix will each hold a 46.5 per cent stake in the JV company, while Berjaya Roasters and Nabil will hold five per cent and two per cent respectively.
The JV company will have a total capital contribution of RM8.64 million.
"Berjaya Roasters shall subscribe for its stake in kinds, i.e., contribute the agreed Kenny Rogers business operational assets including all furniture, fixtures and equipment, whilst the other three shareholders will subscribe their respective equity stake in cash," it said.
Berjaya Roasters will also transfer the restaurants' cash floats and inventories valued at RM41,900 and RM619,209 respectively as at Oct 31, 2026, for which the JV company will reimburse it.
Upon completion of the proposed subscription, the JV company will assume full operational responsibility for the Kenny Rogers business in Malaysia.
"Berjaya Roasters will not be involved in the operational activities relating to the Kenny Rogers restaurants in Malaysia but will continue to provide operational support," it added.
Berjaya Food said the restructuring will reduce its financial and operational commitments to the loss-making business while allowing it to retain a minority stake.
"This will allow the BFood Group to better allocate and deploy its financial and capital resources towards its other food and beverage business operations, thereby enhancing the overall efficiency of its resource utilisation and business portfolio," it said.
Samaya and Vertix are investment holding companies based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), with investments across various sectors, including F&B.
Samaya is also the master franchisee and operator of the Kenny Rogers business in the UAE.
Meanwhile, Nabil is Samaya's group chief financial officer and a board member of Vertix.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wrong car, not robbery attempt, says daughter of elderly 'robber'
Article:
KEPALA BATAS: A viral video alleging an attempted robbery at a petrol station here stemmed from a misunderstanding, says the daughter of an elderly man accused of the act.
Facebook user Siti Nur Nadieya claimed her father had mistaken another vehicle for the red Perodua Alza multi-purpose vehicle their family had rented for four days.
"My father has poor eyesight and did not check the vehicle's registration number at the time of the incident.
"He was supposed to refuel at pump number six, but went to a different pump by mistake. He also assumed the woman refuelling the car was a petrol station attendant.
"He then tried to unlock the vehicle using his remote key fob, and was puzzled when the doors failed to open. He only realised his mistake when the car sped off from the station," she said when contacted today.
The woman said her family was caught off guard when footage of the incident went viral on social media, sparking accusations of an attempted robbery.
"I am lodging a report at the Kepala Batas police headquarters regarding the incident and to refute the viral allegations," she added.
Earlier, a 40-second closed-circuit television (CCTV) clip circulated online showing a woman refuelling her car before an elderly man approached the vehicle.
The woman was seen fleeing the scene, while the driver inside the car sped off after noticing the man trying to open the vehicle's door.
The footage subsequently drew widespread speculation among social media users, who claimed a robbery attempt had taken place at the Jalan Ahmad Badawi station.
Police have yet to receive a report as of press time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No more ‘white, round pills’: MySejahtera’s second life as Malaysia’s digital health hub
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — What began as a mandatory crisis response tool at the height of the Covid-19 pandemic has evolved into the cornerstone of Malaysia’s national digital health infrastructure, serving as a digital front door for millions of residents.
Speaking to Malay Mail, Health Ministry Digital Health Division director Dr Maheshwara Rao Appannan said the MySejahtera application has successfully moved from contact tracing to a comprehensive public health platform, driving the ministry’s “One Person, One Record” vision.
From crisis tool to national platform
At the onset of the pandemic, the government identified a critical need for a digital tool to disseminate information and manage data. Adoption was massive, with nearly 32 million people onboarded.
Dr Maheshwara said inclusivity was key to the strategy.
“It was essential to include everyone residing in the country, not just citizens, because disease knows no boundaries or religion. We utilised that data to strategically identify the areas where vaccination was required most urgently,” he said.
He said Malaysia is now ranked first globally for digital pandemic management by Data.ai, a success that laid the foundation for turning the app into a national public health platform, which currently has between 12 and 15 million monthly active users.
No more “white, round pills”
Historically, patient information in Malaysia was fragmented, and patients moving between public and private facilities often struggled to recall their medical history or specific prescriptions.
Dr Maheshwara said patients frequently described their medication as “white, round pills” rather than by name, a gap the ministry is now closing through MySejahtera.
“Today, over 15 million individuals have their prescriptions and health records accessible within the application.
“With a single click, users can view lab results, dental history and radiological reports,” he said.
“We are empowering users by giving them their records at hand, allowing them to share that information with private practitioners, including both clinics and private hospitals,” he added.
Bridging public and private care
To support this ecosystem, the ministry set up the Malaysia Digital Health Certification Network.
The network currently connects more than 50 private hospitals and over 3,000 general practice clinics, allowing information to flow seamlessly between the public and private sectors while keeping care continuous.
Appointments: Public clinics first
MySejahtera is designed to be a digital front door that reduces the administrative friction often involved in navigating the national healthcare system.
Users can currently schedule appointments directly with public health clinics and dental facilities.
Dr Maheshwara said the booking function is focused on the public sector for now. While the app allows medical records to be shared securely between public and private facilities, appointments with private healthcare providers cannot yet be booked through it.
He said the ministry is actively working to expand these capabilities as part of a broader roadmap to make MySejahtera an all-in-one personal health management tool, allowing patients to manage their entire care journey, from booking to post-visit summaries, on their mobile devices.
Organ pledges go digital
Simplifying organ donor pledges was one of the top priorities in the app’s transformation.
Dr Maheshwara said the previous system relied on paper forms and physical cards, whereas pledges are now recorded in real time. Should a pledger pass away, physicians can immediately verify their donor status in the database.
The app also notifies the pledger’s nominee.
“When a user registers their organ donation pledge, that nominee receives a notification confirming the user’s decision. This is an important step, as it ensures that the next-of-kin is aware of their loved one’s wishes,” he explained.
Looking ahead, the roadmap includes integrating ambulance services into the app. The feature will automatically share a patient’s location during an emergency and link up with the 999 response system for faster, more accurate intervention.
Consent comes first
Addressing data security concerns, Dr Maheshwara stressed that health information is treated as sacred.
He said the platform runs on a consent-driven architecture to build digital trust, and access is never automatic.
There are two main ways to share records. With digital QR consent, users generate a secure, password-protected QR code containing only the information they choose to share with verified practitioners.
Under the explicit consent model, patients must manually approve a doctor’s request to view their historical records through the app, a process similar to approving a bank transfer.
The road to 2029
The ministry aims to fully digitalise all 2,918 primary care facilities and 670 dental facilities with electronic medical records by 2027.
All hospitals nationwide are slated to be fully digitalised by 2029, a longer timeline that reflects the more complex integration required in hospital settings.
Despite the technological leaps, Dr Maheshwara said the technology is merely a vehicle.
He said that in evolving from a pandemic tool into a lifelong health companion, MySejahtera aims to change how Malaysians manage their healthcare needs through their smartphones.

Title: Otters make a splash in KL’s Klang River, bringing hope for cleaner waters — and trouble for fish pond owners
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Beneath a tangle of highway in the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur, a family of otters rolls around in a patch of riverside sand, delighting the few passersby who notice them.
Small groups of otters are now being seen regularly in parts of the city, including along the once heavily polluted Klang River.
Theories vary on whether the smooth-coated otters, classed as vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, have returned to the city or were hiding in plain sight all along.
But their presence has raised hopes that efforts to clean up the Klang may be bearing fruit, and could inspire further improvement.
The Klang was once one of the world’s dirtiest waterways, designated a Class 5 severely polluted river under Malaysia’s rankings.
Years of work improved it to Class 3, or moderately polluted, which seems to have encouraged the otters to move in, said Malaysian wildlife ecologist Woo Chee Yoong.
“Wherever there are otters, there are fish. Wherever there are fish it means the whole river system... (is) clean, it’s healthy for all the communities around. So that’s one of the importance of otters,” he said.
In recent years, the animals have been filmed sunbathing on the river’s concrete banks and swimming in front of elevated metro stations, winning viral fame.
Retired soldier Hasan Ujang, who lives in a riverside apartment, enjoys watching their antics.
“We feel really happy when we watch them playing and playing, like kids swimming,” he said.
‘They have to survive’
But unlike otters in neighbouring Singapore, which are closely monitored by a network of citizen scientists, little is known about Kuala Lumpur’s otters.
Woo learned about them from local media reports on sightings in 2019 and the following year co-founded the Malaysian Otter Network (MON) conservation group.
“We don’t know how many groups are there, we don’t know how actually the otters are moving around,” he said.
Even the question of whether the otters have returned to the capital or were simply in less visible city environments before remains a “mystery.”
MON hopes to set up a citizen science system for people to report sightings.
Otters have been spotted elsewhere in the city, including at the Tropicana Golf & Country Resort, a high-end housing estate where they are less welcome visitors.
They are accused of raiding at least 12 houses in the past year. Their target: fish ponds.
Resident Yee Sze Mun, 89, said otters killed the beloved — and expensive — arowana fish he had nurtured for 15 years.
“They are a nuisance, but I can’t blame them, because they are just like us, they have to survive,” he said.
Residents say the incursions began last year after a company began clearing forest next door for a new development.
“We have an issue because they’re losing their habitat,” said residents’ association president Joy Appukuttan, who called the otter attacks a “grave concern.”
Tropicana’s security team believes there are around 25 otters in the forest and the estate brought in Woo to teach residents how to deal with them.
The species is protected in Malaysia, so Woo urges residents to block entry points to their yards and install fences or netting over ponds.
‘An asset’
Datuk Seri Maimunah Mohd Sharif, a former Kuala Lumpur mayor and now advisor to the city on sustainable urbanisation, call the otters an “asset.”
“Otters are one of the benchmarks for clean cities,” she said.
Like others, she hopes a growing awareness of the Klang River otters can be harnessed to help improve the river further.
Hundreds of garbage traps were installed as part of the government’s River of Life project, and solar-powered “interceptors” deployed by a Dutch NGO have collected tens of thousands of tonnes of waste.
Now Maimunah wants to see more done to stop waste entering the river in the first place, and efforts to make the Klang Class 2B status, clean enough for body contact.
“One day, I want to swim in the Klang River,” she said.
Scarlett Koon Si Qi, a community architect and co-organiser of the annual Klang River Festival hopes the waterway can be restored to its natural banks without concrete lining.
“Some parts, maybe yes, you do need concrete to kind of protect and control for floods,” she said.
“But I think wherever we can, we should leave it as natural as possible.”
That would further benefit the otters, who need some vegetation and natural crevices to hide in, experts said.
The otters are already shifting views on the river, said Faith Foo, who runs the festival.
Growing up, “the teachers would always say that this is a very unsanitary place,” he said.
But seeing the otters, “it’s a reminder that that is a river.” — AFP

Title: Five minutes to Johor: Businesses hope new RTS Link with Singapore brings more than day-trippers
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 24 — If all goes according to plan, the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link will begin operations in February 2027, enhancing connectivity between Singapore and Malaysia, particularly Johor.
With a capacity to carry approximately 40,000 passengers daily and train frequencies of six minutes during off-peak hours and 3.6 minutes during peak periods, the light rail transit shuttle service connecting Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru and Woodlands North in Singapore is expected to generate economic opportunities across various sectors in Johor. The journey between the two stations is expected to take about five minutes.
From small traders to players in the transport and property industries, businesses are hopeful that the RTS Link will boost their earnings by bringing in more visitors from Singapore.
There is, however, another possibility: could the increased cross-border movement lead to Johor Bahru merely serving as a stopover, while the economic benefits are largely confined to businesses operating near the Bukit Chagar RTS station?
Small traders hope to reap benefits
Restaurant owner David Chiang, 65, believes the new rail service will attract more Singaporean customers, not only at weekends but also on weekdays, which are usually quieter.
“When the RTS starts operating, it will be easier for Singaporeans to come to Johor Bahru. They might come for breakfast or lunch, go shopping afterwards and then head straight home,” he told Bernama.
He said Singaporeans already make up a large proportion of the clientele at his restaurant at Jalan Trus here, which has been operating for about 80 years.
Murni Suratman, 51, who has been running a breakfast outlet in Tebrau since 2014, also sees a hike in visitors from Singapore, who generally have greater purchasing power, once the RTS Link is operational.
“It will benefit entrepreneurs, small traders and restaurant operators,” she said.
However, businesses located away from the city centre and popular tourist areas may not benefit to the same extent.
For instance, an asam pedas restaurant operator in Kampung Melayu here, who wished to be identified as Iena, expects visitors to favour established food destinations such as Senibong. Nevertheless, she hopes that upgrading the area surrounding her business premises would help attract new customers.
Traders interviewed by Bernama believe that the economic benefits of the RTS Link will not materialise automatically. Efforts will be needed to promote local products, highlight destinations beyond the established tourist hotspots and strengthen the competitiveness of local businesses.
Encourage overnight stays
While food operators are hoping for an increase in customers, the hospitality industry is endeavouring to turn short visits to Johor Bahru into overnight stays that generate greater visitor spending.
Malaysian Association of Hotels (MAH) Johor Chapter chairman Ivan Teoh said the RTS Link has the potential to benefit all segments of the hospitality industry, including five-star, mid-range and budget hotels, particularly those with convenient access to Bukit Chagar station.
He said hotel occupancy rates in Johor Bahru city centre currently stood at about 90 percent during weekends, with some hotels recording full occupancy during extended holiday periods.
The industry, therefore, expects the RTS Link to not only boost demand during peak periods but also stimulate bookings on weekdays.
“We expect occupancy rates to increase by between 20 and 25 percent during peak seasons,” Teoh said. “Smoother travel may encourage more Singaporeans to make day trips for shopping, dining and entertainment. However, Johor needs to offer more attractive experiences if it wants visitors to stay overnight.”
He believes healthcare and wellness services, medical tourism, diverse food offerings, entertainment and nature-based attractions could serve as additional draws, including for international tourists arriving via Singapore.
Destinations beyond Johor Bahru, such as Tanjung Piai, the various islands and nature-based tourism areas, could also encourage visitors to extend their holidays.
“Therefore, the main opportunity for the hospitality industry lies not merely in attracting more visitors, but in giving them more reasons to stay overnight,” he said.
Cannot sideline local entrepreneurs
Amid the potential growth in the tourism and service industries, questions have also been raised about the participation of local entrepreneurs in the business opportunities arising from the RTS Link development.
Johor Malay Economic Development Chamber president Zaini Atan said the organisation has proposed that at least 30 percent of commercial spaces within the RTS Link station area be allocated to local entrepreneurs, particularly Bumiputeras.
He said the station area is a good platform to introduce local brands to visitors from Singapore and international tourists, rather than being dominated by major business chains.
According to him, local coffee brands such as Kopi Tenggek and Kopi Teman Jiwa have the potential to be showcased as part of Johor’s identity.
“Our concern is that when the station opens, we may not see local companies represented there. Local businesses must be given the opportunity (to promote their products there). Otherwise, tourists may come without getting to see Johor’s own identity,” he said, stressing that all local entrepreneurs should be prioritised, regardless of race, provided that their products and businesses reflect their capabilities as well as the identity of the state.
